_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/26 5:47AM - Good Morning Party People! 6” of fresh fluffy powder came flying down from the sky overnight. It’s looking like a gorgeous day to ski and ride down 57 open trails, of which 54 of those trails received fresh corduroy overnight. Alongside, 13 lifts will be spinning at 8:30 AM, with no anticipated delays. Our mountain ops teams have been hard at work from snowmaking to grooming, that means good things are coming soon, so keep your eyes on the Mountain Report for future information. Have fun, play safe and I'll ski ya out there! 

Safety Tip: Take it easy at the end of the day when you're tired- that is when people get hurt. 

Hungry? Luckily for you, Holiday week is in full swing with extended dining hours, live music, and special events keeping the Village looking lively. Check out our Holiday Week Dining, Après & Live Music Guide to see what's open, happening, and where the music is at.

Spots have opened up this Saturday, the 27th, for a once-in-a-lifetime winter dining experience! Ride a snowcat to our Mid-Mountain Lodge, where a seasonal welcome beverage and hors d’oeuvres lead into a candlelit, six-course dinner crafted by our culinary team. If you can’t make it on Saturday, we have more dates available this winter season. Book now to secure your spot!

The Holidays have arrived at Stratton! The Village is decorated with lights and the schedule is decked with events. Après heats up with live music at Grizzly's, cozy nights at Paint & Sip, and festive fun rolling all week long into a stacked lineup of New Year’s celebrations. Ring it in your way with family dinners, dancing it out at the Silent Disco, hiking up for a one of a kind fireworks view, or watching the fireworks light up the mountain from the base area. There’s something for everyone this Holiday week and we couldn’t be more excited to celebrate with you! Click here to check out the upcoming Events Calendar.

Want to go on an adventure of a lifetime? Well, you're in luck, our Guided Snowmobile Tours are back! Explore Stratton after hours with friends and family on a tour to the summit. Be sure to book your spot now to guarantee it.

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: Snow! We've received 4 inches of new snow in the last 24 hours, including 2 inches overnight. The storm will continue to hit us this morning, with another few inches of snow possible. Apex Express and Moonbeam Express may be delayed this morning as patrol conducts avalanche mitigation work. Sunrise chairlift is now open! Sunrise terrain is ungroomed and limited to North Star and Lower Dynamite. Do not duck ropes into closed terrain, no matter how tempting. Unseen hazards exist and you will lose your pass for at least 30 days (at all Ikon Pass resorts). Due to early season conditions, there is no beginner terrain accessible from Moonbeam Express. Fleet Street is the only route down from Apex Express and should be considered “experts only.” Please check your speed and be aware of other skiers and riders. Holiday fun continues! A DJ will be spinning outside Moonbeam Lodge throughout the weekend. Join us at the Solitude Nordic & Snowshoe Center tonight for our first Nordic Nights of the season.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Laurie  with your 5 am snow report for Saturday, December 27. Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website. 
Our Mid mountain base is 13 inches, the temperature is 30  degrees, the winds are 5 miles per hour from the W, with cloudy skies. 
The Summit base is 19 inches, the temperature is 22 degrees, the winds are 12 miles per hour from the WSW, with cloudy skies.
The base temperature is 39 degrees. 
We will be skiing and riding on 18 lifts, 42 runs, and 302.5 acres on PP/MM snow. 
Looking for a night the whole family will love? Steamboat’s Western BBQ runs all season long and every night this week from December 27th to the 30th. Enjoygreat barbecue, live western music, two-step dance instruction, and kid-friendly activities at 9,000 thousand feet in Thunderhead Lodge. Book ahead at steamboat.com/westernbbq. 
Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  
If you are thinking of exploring outside the ski area boundaries, and don’t know exactly where you are going, don’t go.  
Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: ❗Due to high avalanche danger we are suspending operations today, December 26, 2025. ❗

12/27 7:35 AM Update: Happy Powder Day folks! Winter has returned with power and gusto, and the upper mountain received 8" of new snow overnight and over a foot in the last 24 hours. That, stacked on top of what we were gifted by Mother Nature this week is going to make for some pretty darn good skiing! Turns today will be effortless, and will give you that sweet sweet free-form floating feeling! The forecast calls for light snow and sunbreaks throughout the day.  Although early season conditions still exist widespread around the mountain, there are pockets of deeper snow. Read up on Tree Well and Snow Immersion Safety before heading out on the slopes, and please take it easy out there, especially in higher traffic areas.

Rafters opens today at 10:30am to 8pm with hybrid table service.  See below for complete F+B Hours for today. Our first Rafters Happy Hour of the season is on from 3-5pm! Come by for games, specials, and music by Pretty Funk Dub from 3pm to 5pm! Night skiing continues until 8pm as well. It's Holiday Central on the hill this week. Come on up!

We have returned to regular access and our standard parking plan. Read the SPECIAL OPERATIONS UPDATE below for more details. 

Notes for today:
  1. Ski & ride with care. We know you’re excited, and we are too. Please ride responsibly and stay in control today as we launch the 2025-2026 Winter Season. Brush up on Mountain Safety and the Responsibility Code!
  2. Obey all mountain closures. Our team is working hard to open terrain as quickly and safely as possible. Closed areas are closed for a reason, so please keep yourself and our team safe by only skiing in open areas.
  3. As a reminder, when being added from the parking waitlist, cancellations are still required if you're not planning on making it up. Thank you!
  4. At this time, paid reservations can only be cancelled by emailing SP+ at  CrystalMtnParking@spplus.com with Reservation #, First Name, and Last Name. The Crystal Mountain Contact center cannot process these cancellations.

Mountain Weather 12/26/2025 4:20pm 
 
Synopsis:  A short wave trough is making its way through the mountain territories this afternoon into the evening.  This will mark the end of 3+ weeks of very active weather.  We can look forward to a healthy shot of precip into tomorrow.  With very cold temps in place and a favorable atmospheric setup, things could stack up with great liquid to snow ratios.  Ridgelines will see a healthy dose of WNW winds.  This bodes well for Crystal as it places us on the northern end of the Great Tahoma block.  By Saturday afternoon we can look forward to upper elevation sunshine and diminishing winds.  The Valley’s will likely cling onto thick cloud cover and I would expect icy conditions to form on roadways.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
December 27th, 9:59 AM
*North Lynx hiking will be delayed*
Good morning skiers and riders, and happy holidays! Mother Nature is in full holiday spirit, delivering another 3 inches of fresh snow across the mountain. Today's forecast calls for a slight rise in temperatures, expect mid to low 20's at the base and mid to low teens at the summit. Look forward to dancing on 38 machine groomed runs, paired with packed powder conditions on natural terrain, all garnished with a layer of fresh snow. Snowmaking will be finishing up on Racer's Edge and Lower Snowball and moving over towards Stein's. Cruiser, Riemergasse, and the Times Square area at Mt. Ellen will continue snowmaking. Saddle up your sleighs, we’re expecting several snowy days during the holiday week, which could bring over 12 inches of fresh snow as we head into the New Year!

We will be getting down on 460 skiable acres served by 12 lifts and 106 open trails. Ropes have dropped on loads of natural terrain, please use caution as coverage is thin and suggested for experts only. Hiking for North Lynx is open from 10:00 AM - 3:00 PM today. Plus, Castlerock lift will be spinning 9:00 AM- 3:45 PM. Whether you're looking for easy laid-back groomers or leg burning moguls, we've got it all.

Operations have shifted to holiday hours, which means GMX, Super Bravo and Heaven's Gate will get the party started at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. The Sugarbush Parks crew has assembled a bumping freestyle setup at Mt. Ellen with 15 features and 2 jumps. Plus, Slowpoke at Lincoln Peak is home to 4 features, and newly installed side hits! Join us Dec 24th - Jan 1st, for our Holiday Week at Sugarbush, filled with skiing, riding, and festive events for the whole family. Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill travel routes are now open at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen, check out our uphill travel policy for more info.

Bonjour Tremblant!

After a snowy holiday buildup, the mountain is ready to deliver one of those classic bluebird days.

Mother Nature is shifting gears and delivering something special today. Milder temperatures, a big bright sun, and almost no wind. That's the kind of weather made for smooth turns, fast laps, and endless cruisers.

The 40 cm of snow we received over the past week during the holiday period has set us up beautifully. Thanks to that natural boost and the incredible work of our mountain ops team, 90% of our skiable terrain is now open, representing 279 hectares ready to explore.

Conditions are prime across the mountain. Alpine touring is open, and both Progression Park and Mitik Park are welcoming riders with solid coverage and smooth features.

Blue skies, softening temps, and wide-open terrain. It’s one of those days that reminds you why winter on the mountain is so special. Get out there and enjoy every turn!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users. Here are a few tips for a safe experience:

• Familiarize yourself with the lift before using it and pay attention.
• Ask the ski lift attendant if you are unfamiliar with how it works.
• Follow the rules posted along the lift route.
• Watch the chairlift safety video: Vidéo utilisation sécuritaire télésiège
 
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
